To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibition of Slug expression by small interfering RNA enhances oral squamous cell carcinomas sensitivity to X-ray radiation through upregulating the expression of P53 upregulated modulator of apoptosis.
inhibition of Slug expression by small interfering RNA increases radiosensitivity of HSC3 or HSC6 cells by upregulation of PUMA.
inhibition of Slug expression in oral squamous cell carcinomas by siRNA increases the expression of Puma, which contributes to radiosensitivity of HSC3 cells toward X-ray radiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiosensitivity of oral cancer cells and provides an experimental basis for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
the radiosensitivity of oral cancer cells by Slug and PUMA.
the potential application of Slug siRNA as a novel radiosensitizer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Slug inhibition increases radiosensitivity by upregulating puma.
Slug siRNA could be used to increase sensitivity of oral squamous cells toward X-ray radiation.
inhibition of Slug expression increases radiosensitivity of OSCC cells by upregulation of PUMA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Slug siRNA transfections in combination with radiotherapy could be used as a new strategy for the treatment of OSCC.
the combination of radiotherapy with Slug siRNA transduction could be a novel therapeutic approach to improve the treatment of oral squamous cancer.
Slug inhibition increased radiosensitivity of oral cancer cells by upregulation of PUMA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Slug is a potential target for radio-gene therapy.
Slug siRNA can increase radiosensitivity of oral cancer cells in vitro, and Slug siRNA transduction combined with radiotherapy may be a potential therapeutic approach for oral cancer.
Slug siRNA could be an effective strategy to increase radiosensitivity of oral cancer cells.
